chunks: And it is narrated from Abū al-Rabīʿ, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who cultivates in another man's land on the condition that one-third is for the cattle, one-third is for the seed, and one-third is for the owner of the land.

So he عليه السلام said: He should not designate cattle or seed, but rather he should say to the owner of the land: I will cultivate your land, and for you is such-and-such from what Allah, Mighty and Glorious, brings forth in it.

key_terms.أَخْرَجَ اللَّهُ: what Allah brings forth from the land as produce
key_terms.أُزَارِعُكَ: I enter into a cultivation/sharecropping arrangement with you
key_terms.بَقَرًا: cattle used in the farming process

ai.seo_question: How should a valid sharecropping agreement be worded in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on sharecropping arrangements. It teaches that the agreement should assign a share of the produce to the landowner without tying fixed portions separately to cattle and seed, thereby framing the contract around the actual crop produced by Allah عزّ وجلّ.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3904 - It is narrated from Abu Al-Rabi', from Abu Abdillah (as), regarding a man who cultivates another man's land on the condition that one-third is allocated for the oxen, one-third for the seeds, and one-third for the landowner.

Imam (as) said: "He should not specify shares for the oxen or the seeds. Instead, he should say to the landowner, 'I will cultivate your land, and you will receive such-and-such portion of what Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, produces from it.'"
